title: Everyday-life intergenerational regenerative formation scan
purpose: Recenter active discovery on visible everyday-life latent-value fields between younger people and newly/relatively young retired adults, rather than industrial/internal-enterprise examples.

formation_family.name: Young people × retired/low-age older adults everyday mutual-value field
formation_family.description: Two large and continuously replenishing populations hold complementary everyday resources: retired adults often have time, rooms/space, childcare/life experience, craft/local knowledge and desire for usefulness; younger people often have digital ability, mobility, design/media fluency and need affordable housing, childcare relief, local-life knowledge, community belonging and trusted support. Reality already creates multiple cross-generational partial flows, usually under community/institutional trust scaffolding.
formation_family.cross_domain_missing_edge_hypothesis: Unrelated generations may lack a low-friction, trusted, bounded and reciprocal exchange infrastructure that makes everyday value safely callable outside kinship or institution-led projects.
formation_family.warning: Do not collapse distinct life domains into one platform thesis unless the same missing edge is independently observed across them.

formation_zones.name: Spare housing / affordable youth living × companionship and everyday support

state_pressure: loneliness/limited social circle for some older adults
underused institutional or household space in some contexts

durable_endowments: ability to participate in low-risk non-professional support
state_pressure: need for affordable housing and community belonging

observed_partial_flows.fact: Shanghai's 2026 civil-affairs response accepted proposals for intergenerational co-living / volunteer service exchanged for housing benefits, explicitly connecting elderly companionship needs with youth housing pressure.
Changzhou public eldercare institution launched a 2026 '志愿服务换住房' model: young residents aged 22-40 can receive free or discounted rooms in exchange for 10-20 hours/month of volunteer service.
Suzhou eldercare institutions have operated youth co-living models where young workers pay only a small monthly amount and provide companionship/teaching/support hours.

formation_zones.missing_edge_hypothesis: Trust, resident-fit screening, privacy, liability, service-boundary definition and continuity may prevent ordinary older homeowners/institutions and unrelated young people from forming the relationship without a trusted organizer.
kill_conditions: if institutional co-living already scales sufficiently without a new recurring edge
if household-level trust/privacy/liability cannot be standardized
if economics rely mainly on public subsidy rather than mutual surplus

formation_zones.name: Retired time/care experience × young dual-income family time scarcity

durable_endowments: desire for usefulness and social participation

state_pressure: dual-income parents repeatedly face pickup/after-school supervision gaps

observed_partial_flows.fact: Hangzhou/Ningbo and other cities operate 'shared grandma' teams. In one community, 50-65 year-old retirees use shifts to pick up children; another team had delivered 3,472 child-service instances by end-2024.
A 2026 report describes the persistent '4:30 problem' for dual-income families and ongoing shared-grandma pickup/after-school support.
Some shared-grandma models now include family '反哺联盟': beneficiary families later deliver groceries/repairs to older residents, creating a reciprocal loop instead of one-way volunteering.

recurring_event_source: ongoing inflow of newly retired healthy adults
formation_zones.missing_edge_hypothesis: Outside close kin/community, trust, child-safety responsibility, identity screening, scheduling, insurance/liability, emergency authority and reciprocity accounting may block this abundant time-resource from circulating.
kill_conditions: if safety/liability makes externalized circulation structurally unsuitable
if childcare licensing/professional boundaries absorb the useful scope
if the exchange only works as tightly local voluntary community governance

formation_zones.name: Retired life/local/craft knowledge × youth digital capability and reciprocal learning

state_pressure: need for belonging and cross-generational experience

observed_partial_flows.fact: Shanghai Changning launched 'exchange skills with 100 elders': young participants wanted Shanghai dialect, market-shopping skills, knitting and woodwork; older participants wanted smartphone use and video editing.
In 2026 communities, elders teach zongzi wrapping, tai chi, calligraphy and traditional skills while young people teach video creation and digital skills.

In Xuzhou, Jiangsu Safety Technical Vocational College and Jiurucheng created '青银搭档': students teach video calls, a retired carpenter teaches woodwork, and a retired engineer works with students to turn 'old Xuzhou memories' into short videos.
A national youth digital-support organization has grown to 20,000+ volunteers, 100+ universities and 500+ communities, showing the digital-help flow is not isolated.

recurring_event_source: ongoing desire for practical/life skill learning
ongoing older-adult desire for digital autonomy
formation_zones.missing_edge_hypothesis: Useful reciprocal skills are highly fragmented and invisible; outside organized activities, unrelated generations lack persistent discovery, trust, matching, reciprocity and continuation mechanisms.
kill_conditions: if participants value only social/volunteer context and resist economic exchange
if matching frequency is too low to create a Demand Pump
if generic interest/community platforms already solve discovery sufficiently

formation_zones.name: Retired craft/life production × youth design, storytelling and distribution

state_pressure: early-career creators often lack rooted supply and stories

observed_partial_flows.fact: Shaoxing's West Lake basket collaboration has run for six years: an elder could spend 5-6 hours weaving a basket that sold for RMB 6 with little demand; youth redesign/branding/distribution lifted the average price to RMB 60 with demand exceeding supply.
The same model splits roles: elders weave, young social workers/students design packaging and sell/promote through scenic retail, short video and livestreaming; 80% of proceeds return to artisans.

Shanghai's 'retirement market' links retired makers with young design/retail operators; organisers report older makers have solid technique while young people bring creativity and flexible resources, with the concept expanding to other cities/pop-ups.
Beijing's '银发匠人' projects explicitly use a chain from artisan discovery to product conversion, income-generating sales and transmission.

recurring_event_source: ongoing youth demand for differentiated cultural products
formation_zones.missing_edge_hypothesis: Large amounts of senior craft/life-production capacity may be economically stranded because product reframing, design, story, aggregation, quality consistency and distribution are separated from production capability.
kill_conditions: if only a tiny subset of aesthetically marketable crafts works
if youth design/distribution contribution is easily disintermediated
if the recurring supply/demand field is too fragmented to standardize

cross_zone_pattern.observed: Across housing, childcare, reciprocal skills and craft commercialization, cross-generational value flows repeatedly become workable only after a trusted community/institution/social-organization layer supplies screening, matching, rules, space, scheduling, accountability or reciprocity accounting.
cross_zone_pattern.hypothesis: The deeper recurring edge may be 'trusted relationship infrastructure for non-kin intergenerational exchange', rather than any one service category.
falsification_questions: Do comparable flows emerge spontaneously at scale without trusted organizers?
Are the blockers actually domain-specific (housing law, childcare safety, craft distribution) rather than one shared edge?
Do younger and older participants want reciprocal/economic exchange outside community/volunteer settings?
Does the organizer retain recurring value after the first match?
Can one trust/identity/reciprocity layer generalize without becoming a broad generic marketplace?

next_action: Do a cross-domain missing-edge discrimination pass across LWF-001..004. Test whether the recurring dependency on community/institution scaffolding is evidence of one shared trust/relationship infrastructure gap or merely four unrelated domain-specific barriers. Search failures, bypass behavior, participant motivations, safety/liability boundaries and repeatability. Do not design a platform or price a service.
